claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires solid-state sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 has inherent or significant porosity and microstructural imperfections.
A liquid-phase precursor method can prepare nanoscale, fine, and uniform ZrB2 particles.
Combining liquid-phase precursor synthesis with SPS will produce single-phase ZrB2 at 1800–2000 °C.
SPS provides rapid consolidation and can substantially shorten processing time.
Rapid SPS consolidation of nanoscale ZrB2 powder will enhance densification.
Rapid SPS consolidation of nanoscale ZrB2 powder will create a more uniform grain structure.
The proposed precursor-SPS route will reduce pore and defect formation in ZrB2.
Fine, uniform precursor-derived powders sinter rapidly under SPS and thereby promote a homogeneous, low-porosity ZrB2 microstructure.
Lower porosity and improved microstructural integrity will enhance resistance to chemical and mechanical degradation during prolonged liquid plating bath exposure.
Relative to conventionally sintered ZrB2, the proposed material will contain fewer pores and holes.
Relative to conventionally sintered ZrB2, the proposed material will have improved mechanical strength.
Relative to conventionally sintered ZrB2, the proposed material will have a longer service life in a liquid plating bath.
Porosity and structural imperfections in conventional ZrB2 lead to lower durability during long-term liquid exposure.
Extended liquid plating bath exposure causes pore or hole formation and eventual failure in conventionally prepared ZrB2.
